decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark — enter a URL, optional title & tags; it appears in the list.” Round 1 client retained URL saving and tag assignment while requesting additions.
decisions.note: The presented URL-save and tag-assignment behavior conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered only an “optional title” and editing of “titles/tags.” Round 1 client required collected title and description to remain editable and later clarified this meant before and after saving.
decisions.note: The initial specification omitted editable description and complete pre/post-save editing; the client extended it at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “find links by keyword across title, address, and tags.” Round 1 client required descriptions, notes, case-insensitivity, `#tag`, exact phrases, AND/OR/NOT, and parentheses.
decisions.note: The initial basic search was materially short of the reference search behavior; the client supplied the missing scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete — correct titles/tags.” Round 1 client required an editable address, description, and note as well as title and tags.
decisions.note: The initial editable field set was incomplete; the client extended it at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “remove with confirmation.” Round 1 client did not contest deletion and later required permanent delete alongside archive.
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark removal was present and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Organize with tags — filter the list down to one tag.” Round 1 client retained tag-based filtering.
decisions.note: Filtering to a selected tag conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only “derives a title when none is given” and sets “no page-preview fetching” as a boundary. Round 1 client required automatic title, description, site icon, and preview image collection.
decisions.note: Automatic metadata collection was substantially incomplete; the client supplied the complete reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Opens destinations in a new tab.” No client response contested this behavior.
decisions.note: Opening the original destination in a new tab is functionally equivalent to the required navigation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker promised only that the app “Warns on duplicate URLs.” Round 1 client: “Saving the same address takes me to the existing bookmark to update it; it must not allow a second copy.”
decisions.note: A warning does not ensure convergence to editing or prevent duplication; the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope mentioned entering and editing tags but no suggestions. Round 1 client: “Existing tags are suggested while I type.”
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete was missing from the initial scope and was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s stated v1 scope omitted read-later state and views. Round 1 client required marking links for later, a separate list, and marking them read.
decisions.note: The client extended the initial specification with the complete read-later workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s stated v1 scope included deletion but no archive. Round 1 client required non-destructive archive, a separate archive view, and restoration.
decisions.note: The archive lifecycle and distinction from deletion were missing and added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s v1 scope had no bulk operations. Round 1 client required selecting multiple links or all links matching the current search/filter for tag, archive, read-state, or delete actions.
decisions.note: Both selected-item and whole-filtered-collection bulk actions were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker said a saved bookmark merely “appears in the list.” Round 1 client required each item to clearly show title, description, tags, and site icon.
decisions.note: The readability-first item contents were absent from the initial presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s scope did not include sorting. Round 1 client: “I can sort the list.”
decisions.note: List sorting was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s stated scope omitted saved filters. Round 1 client required saving combinations of searches and included or excluded tags for reuse.
decisions.note: Reusable bundles were missing and added at the initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered “No sync / no import-export in v1 — okay to defer?” Round 1 client required import and export of standard browser bookmark files and said “please don’t defer that.”
decisions.note: The maker offered a nonconforming deferral and the client selected the reference-conforming inclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 v1 scope omitted preservation. Round 1 client required a local copy, PDFs kept as PDFs, and optional Internet Archive preservation.
decisions.note: Both local and Internet Archive preservation were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s scope omitted display settings. Round 1 client required default sorting, item count, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only floated notes as a possible missed feature. Round 1 client required an editable note and stated: “Notes should support simple formatting when displayed.”
decisions.note: Markdown-capable bookmark notes were made a requirement by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: metadata fetches title, description, site icon, and preview image; “title & description stay editable.” Round 2 client did not contest these points.
decisions.note: The revised specification conformed on automatic metadata and editable collected fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker proposed deduplication that drops trailing slashes and tracking parameters. Round 2 client said those may identify genuinely different pages and required only safely equivalent addresses to deduplicate.
decisions.note: The proposed normalization could merge distinct reference-domain bookmarks; the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented editable address/title/tags/description/note, tag suggestions, and safely rendered lightweight Markdown. Round 2 client explicitly said the note approach was fine and did not contest the field set or suggestions.
decisions.note: The revised richer-bookmark behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified case-insensitive search over title/description/note/address, `#tag`, and exact phrases. Round 2 client said the overall search order was fine and requested only the literal-operator rule.
decisions.note: These revised search capabilities conform independently of the separate operator-literal omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and precedence but did not state how to search operator words literally. Round 2 client required that “AND,” “OR,” and “NOT” be searchable literally when quoted.
decisions.note: The boolean grammar omitted a required edge rule; the client added it.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented a separate read-later list with independent read/unread state. Round 2 client did not request a change.
decisions.note: The revised read-later workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented archive without deletion, a separate archive view, restore, and permanent delete. Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised archive lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: select items or “all matching current search/filter” for tag, archive, read/unread, and delete actions. Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Both bulk-action scopes conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified sorting and item display of title, description, tags, and site icon. Round 2 client did not contest these points.
decisions.note: The revised list presentation and sorting conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented reusable named queries with included/excluded tags. Round 2 client did not request a change.
decisions.note: The saved-filter bundle behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified standard browser import and folder-to-tag mapping but did not state preservation of all required metadata. Round 2 client required preservation of title, tags, and original date-added where present.
decisions.note: Import metadata preservation was incomplete and the client supplied the missing rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented export in the standard Netscape bookmark HTML format. Round 2 client said that format was fine.
decisions.note: The export format conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker promised a “Local copy (PDFs saved as PDFs)” without defining the HTML artifact. Round 2 client required “a self-contained HTML file representing the original page, not merely an extracted readable version.”
decisions.note: The local-copy representation was underspecified relative to the reference and was corrected by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included an optional Internet Archive snapshot with graceful failure. Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified persistent default sort, items shown, and text size. Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised display preferences conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker discussed tag editing and suggestions but presented no uniqueness constraint. Round 2 client: “Please ensure two tags with the same name cannot be created for this collection.”
decisions.note: The reference Tag entity’s uniqueness constraint was missing and was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker claimed deduplication was corrected, but Round 3 client found the edge-cases section still said trailing slashes and tracking parameters were duplicates and requested alignment with the narrowed rule.
decisions.note: This later revised presentation remained internally divergent; the client caught the residual contradiction.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker added quoted literal searches for “AND,” “OR,” and “NOT.” Round 3 client said everything except the duplicate edge-case now looked right.
decisions.note: The corrected literal-operator rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker retained the client-approved lightweight Markdown approach. Round 3 client reported no further note issue.
decisions.note: The note-formatting decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker stated import preserves title, tags, and original date-added where present. Round 3 client reported no further import issue.
decisions.note: The corrected import behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specified self-contained HTML representing the original page and PDFs stored as PDFs. Round 3 client reported no further preservation issue.
decisions.note: The corrected local preservation behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specified case-insensitive unique tag names and reuse of an existing tag. Round 3 client reported no further tag issue.
decisions.note: The corrected tag uniqueness constraint conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker replaced the contradictory edge case with safely equivalent host-case/default-port matching while keeping trailing-slash and query variants separate. Round 4 client approved the specification.
decisions.note: The final specification’s duplicate rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned Playwright/Chromium for rendered metadata and faithful self-contained HTML, with PDFs saved as PDFs. Round 5 client said the plan preserved the agreed behaviors.
decisions.note: The metadata and local-preservation plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned the Internet Archive Save Page Now endpoint and storage of its snapshot reference. Round 5 client approved the plan.
decisions.note: The Internet Archive plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned a parser supporting `#tag`, phrases, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and quoted literal operators. Round 5 client approved.
decisions.note: The planned advanced-query syntax conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned a canonical key that lowercases the host and drops only the default port, retaining slash and query variants. Round 5 client approved.
decisions.note: The implementation plan’s duplicate rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned Netscape HTML import/export preserving title, tags, and date-added. Round 5 client approved.
decisions.note: The import/export plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker planned Markdown storage with sanitized rendering. Round 5 client approved.
decisions.note: The note implementation plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker said the React interface would handle tag autocomplete and a multi-select bulk bar. Round 5 client approved React/Vite and the behavior-preserving plan.
decisions.note: The planned autocomplete and multi-selection interactions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned the save-with-auto-metadata story to tasks T015–T021. Round 6 client said the breakdown covered the agreed behavior and approved implementation.
decisions.note: The task decision for URL saving and metadata collection conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned “No duplicates / open existing” to T022–T025. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The duplicate-handling task decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned editable fields, formatted notes, unique tags, and suggestions to T026–T031. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The richer bookmark and tag task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned advanced boolean search to T032–T037. Round 6 client said the tasks covered the agreed behavior.
decisions.note: The advanced-search task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned read-later to T038–T040. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The read-later task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned archive/restore to T041–T043. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The archive task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned bulk actions to T044–T046. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The bulk-action task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned sort and presentation to T047–T049. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The list presentation and sorting task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned saved searches to T050–T052. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The bundle task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned import/export to T053–T057. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The import/export task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned page preservation to T058–T062. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The preservation task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assigned display preferences to T063–T065. Round 6 client approved.
decisions.note: The display-preference task group conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported save with metadata and a backend metadata-fetch library. Round 7 client’s correction concerned review/edit before saving, not URL saving or metadata collection.
decisions.note: The implemented save and metadata portions conform independently of the pre-save editing defect.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presented the implementation as complete, but Round 7 client observed: “the current save area only accepts an address and immediately saves it” and required review/edit of collected title and description before saving.
decisions.note: The implementation omitted the required pre-save editing stage; the client corrected it during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported an edit modal and safe note rendering; Round 7 client explicitly acknowledged editing title and description afterward already existed and requested only the pre-save correction.
decisions.note: Post-save editing and formatted-note behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported bookmark CRUD and delete in per-item/bulk actions. Round 7 client raised no deletion defect and later accepted the application.
decisions.note: Deletion was presented as implemented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker verified deduplication of host-case/default-port equivalents, distinct slash/query variants, and 409 on edit to an existing URL. Round 7 client raised no duplicate defect.
decisions.note: The implemented duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported live advanced search and verified `#tag`, phrases, boolean operators, parentheses, and quoted literal operators. Round 7 client raised no search defect.
decisions.note: The implemented advanced-search decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported read-later tabs and read-state actions. Round 7 client raised no read-later defect and later accepted the app.
decisions.note: The implemented read-later workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported archive/restore, a separate archive tab, and delete actions, including verified persistence of archive state. Round 7 client raised no archive defect.
decisions.note: The implemented archive lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported multi-select actions, “select all matching,” and verified “archive all matching.” Round 7 client raised no bulk-action defect.
decisions.note: The implemented selected-item and current-filter bulk behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported and verified tag suggestions. Round 7 client raised no autocomplete defect.
decisions.note: The implemented tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported a frontend sort control. Round 7 client raised no sorting defect and later accepted the app.
decisions.note: The implemented list sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported saved searches with include/exclude tag filters and verified persistence over a cold restart. Round 7 client raised no bundle defect.
decisions.note: The implemented reusable saved-filter behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported import/export and verified folder and `TAGS` handling, preserved ADD_DATE, duplicate skipping, and summary output. Round 7 client raised no import/export defect.
decisions.note: The implemented Netscape import/export behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported self-contained-HTML/PDF capture and verified that a local self-contained HTML file was written. Round 7 client raised no preservation-format defect.
decisions.note: The implemented local preservation behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported an Internet Archive submission library and UI preservation controls with graceful external failure. Round 7 client raised no Internet Archive defect.
decisions.note: The Internet Archive capability was presented as implemented consistently with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker reported preferences and verified that they survived a cold restart. Round 7 client raised no preference defect.
decisions.note: The implemented display preferences conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented URL “Fetch details” without saving, a review panel for editing collected title/description, explicit Save/Cancel, and continued post-save editing. Round 8 client: “this matches the approved behavior.”
decisions.note: The revised two-step save flow and before/after editing conform at final implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker stated that a duplicate detected during preview opens the existing bookmark to edit and creates no second copy. Round 8 client accepted the completed application.
decisions.note: The corrected preview flow preserves reference-conforming duplicate handling.
